Both the OpenAI and Anthropic paths are confirmed working through the Router simulator, and the inactive-Router case confirms the documented no-op contract (`routerFetch(undefined)` returns `undefined` exactly as it did before, since `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` is unset).

## Summary

**Context:** this is a desktop Obsidian plugin, not a backend service. Every one of its 13 LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Google, xAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, Groq, generic OpenAI-format, SiliconFlow, Copilot Plus, Mistral, DeepSeek) is BYOK — the end user types their own key into the plugin's settings UI on their own machine. There are no application-held provider secrets anywhere in the repo (no `.env` files, no CI secrets referencing `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). The vendored `src/lib/routerRuntime.ts` shim (already wired into `ChatOpenRouter.ts` by the prior codemod) is a `fetch`-level interceptor: it's a complete no-op unless `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` is set in the environment, and even when active it only intercepts requests whose *host* is `api.openai.com` or `api.anthropic.com` — everything else passes straight to its original destination.

**What I migrated:** `src/LLMProviders/chatModelManager.ts` builds the LangChain client config for every provider. Two of those — `OPENAI` (`ChatOpenAI`, defaults to `api.openai.com`) and `ANTHROPIC` (`ChatAnthropic`, defaults to `api.anthropic.com`) — were still constructed with a bare `fetch: customModel.enableCors ? safeFetchNoThrow : undefined`, bypassing the shim entirely (unlike `ChatOpenRouter`, which already wraps its fetch with `routerFetch`). I wrapped both with `routerFetch(...)`, matching the existing pattern. Verified with standalone smoke requests against the Router simulator: a Chat-Completions-shaped OpenAI call and an Anthropic Messages call both got intercepted, had their `Authorization`/`x-api-key` header replaced with `Bearer $RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY` (the user-supplied key never left the process), were translated to `POST /v1/responses` / `POST /v1/messages`, and came back with valid 200 responses from the simulator.

**Call sites I did not migrate, and why:**
- Every other provider's client (Cohere, Google, xAI, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-format, SiliconFlow, Mistral, DeepSeek) constructs its request against that provider's own distinct host, which `routerRuntime.ts`'s host allowlist (`api.openai.com` / `api.anthropic.com` only) never matches — wrapping their `fetch` would be a dead no-op, so I left them untouched rather than add inert code.
- `COPILOT_PLUS` (`ChatOpenRouter` pointed at `models.brevilabs.com`) is the plugin vendor's own hosted backend, authenticated with a `plusLicenseKey`, not a provider API key. The actual model calls happen server-side on Brevilabs' infrastructure, which this repo has no visibility into — there's nothing here to point at Router.
- Embeddings, model-listing/credential-verification calls (`GET /models` in the `modelManagement/providers/adapters/*` files), and local-provider traffic (Ollama/LM Studio to `localhost`) are correctly left on the direct provider path — the shim explicitly carves these out (embeddings/images/files bypass Router by design; GET-based listing isn't one of the two intercepted routes).

No env files, secrets, or CI config needed changes (none existed to begin with — confirmed by grep). `npm run build`'s typecheck passes and the full unit suite (569 suites / 7867 tests) passes unchanged.
